description: Cross-field consistency rules — rules for checking that finding fields are internally consistent. Sourced from review_taxonomy.yaml (consistency_rules).

entries.title: Reported severity should align with CVSS score range
entries.description: The reported severity level should fall within the range implied by the CVSS score. For example, CVSS 8.5 implies High severity (7.0-8.9 range). If the reported severity is Medium for CVSS 8.5, this is a mismatch that should be flagged.
conditions: reported severity does not match CVSS score range
entries.action: Flag as severity-CVSS mismatch (taxonomy SEV). Report both reported severity and CVSS-implied severity. Do NOT auto-correct.

entries.title: Classification must not be Confirmed if evidence is insufficient
entries.description: If the evidence is insufficient (EVID_INSUFF, EVID_NONE, or EVID_SCANNER_ONLY), the classification must NOT be confirmed_vulnerability. The consistency check overrides the classification to potential_issue when this rule is violated.
entries.action: Override classification to potential_issue. Flag as evidence-classification inconsistency (taxonomy CLASS). This is an override, not a suggestion.

entries.title: Finding title should reflect the described vulnerability
entries.description: The finding title should be consistent with the observation and evidence content. A title describing 'SQL Injection' with evidence showing 'XSS' indicates a title-content mismatch. This is flagged for human review.
conditions: title describes different vulnerability than evidence
entries.action: Flag as title-content mismatch. Flag for human review. Do NOT auto-correct title.

entries.title: Recommendation should address root cause, not just symptoms
entries.description: The recommendation should be consistent with the root cause described in the observation. A finding about 'insecure deserialization' with a recommendation to 'update TLS certificates' is inconsistent — the recommendation addresses a different issue.
conditions: recommendation addresses different issue than observation
recommendation is tangential to root cause
entries.action: Flag as recommendation-cause mismatch. Flag for human review to write appropriate remediation.
